summary_md: **Steins ([@FooSteins](https://x.com/FooSteins/status/2116733022267666630))** explains **L3G-World** from KAIST AI by Choi et al. ([arXiv 2610.40614](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40614), [project](https://cvlab-kaist.github.io/L3G-World/)): from one image it generates a walkable world in real time at 9 FPS, remembering what is behind you via 3D Gaussians storing VAE latents that render straight into the DiT's latent space; the thread cites up to 38.6x fewer primitives and 359x faster memory rendering than prior 3D memory.

media.description: Side-by-side of generated world video and its 3D Gaussian memory.
L3G-World overview: a single image, text prompt and camera trajectory feed a latent 3D Gaussian memory, with L3G-Gen and L3G-Mem modules enabling infinite world generation.
Architecture of L3G-Gen, an autoregressive video DiT conditioned on rendered persistent memory, with memory-conditioned generation examples.
Architecture of L3G-Mem and a visualization of memory updates with spawn masks.
L3G-World overview with charts showing flat memory use and steady real-time throughput over generation time, while baselines run out of memory.
Qualitative comparison grid of L3G-World and L3G-World Fast against Matrix-Game 3.0, Yume 1.5, GEN3C, Spatia, Lyra 2.0 and NeoVerse across three scenes.
